passages.text: All farmers growing notified crops in a notified area during the season who have insurable interest in the crop are eligible.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 3, para 7 Farmers to be covered

passages.text:
To provide insurance coverage and financial support to the farmers in the event of failure of any of the notified crop as a result of natural calamities, pests & diseases.
To stabilise the income of farmers to ensure their continuance in farming.
To encourage farmers to adopt innovative and modern agricultural practices.
To ensure flow of credit to the agriculture sector.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 1, para 1 Objectives

passages.text:
The enrolment under the scheme, subject to possession of insurable interest on the cultivation of the notified crop in the notified area, shall be compulsory for following categories of farmers:
Farmers in the notified area who possess a Crop Loan account/KCC account (called as Loanee Farmers) to whom credit limit is sanctioned/renewed for the notified crop during the crop season.
Such other farmers whom the Government may decide to include from time to time.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 4, para 7.1 Compulsory coverage

passages.text: Voluntary coverage may be obtained by all farmers not covered in 7.1 above, including Crop KCC/Crop Loan Account holders whose credit limit is not renewed.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 4, para 7.2 Voluntary coverage

passages.text:
Comprehensive risk insurance is provided to cover yield losses due to non-preventable risks, such as
Natural Fire and Lightning
Storm, Hailstorm, Cyclone, Typhoon, Tempest, Hurricane, Tornado etc.
Flood, Inundation and Landslide
Drought, Dry spells
Pests/ Diseases etc.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 4, para 8.1.1 Risks, yield losses

passages.text: In cases where majority of the insured farmers of a notified area, having intent to sow/plant and incurred expenditure for the purpose, are prevented from sowing/planting the insured crop due to adverse weather conditions, shall be eligible for indemnity claims upto a maximum of 25% of the sum-insured.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 5, para 8.1.2 Risks, prevented sowing

passages.text: Coverage is available upto a maximum period of 14 days from harvesting for those crops which are kept in “cut & spread” condition to dry in the field after harvesting, against specific perils of cyclone / cyclonic rains, unseasonal rains throughout the country.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 5, para 8.1.3 Risks, post-harvest losses

passages.text: Loss / damage resulting from occurrence of identified localized risks i.e. hailstorm, landslide, and Inundation affecting isolated farms in the notified area.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 5, para 8.1.4 Risks, localised calamities

passages.text: Risks and Losses arising out of following perils shall be excluded:- War & kindred perils, nuclear risks, riots, malicious damage, theft, act of enmity, grazed and/or destroyed by domestic and/or wild animals, In case of Post–Harvest losses the harvested crop bundled and heaped at a place before threshing, other preventable risks.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 5, para 8.2 Exclusions

passages.text:
In case of Loanee farmers under Compulsory Component, the Sum Insured would be equal to Scale of Finance for that crop as fixed by District Level Technical Committee (DLTC) which may extend up to the value of the threshold yield of the insured crop at the option of insured farmer.
For farmers covered on voluntary basis the sum-insured is upto the value of Threshold yield i.e threshold yield x (MSP or gate price) of the insured crop.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; pp. 5-6, para 9 Sum insured

passages.text:
Kharif Food & Oilseeds crops (all cereals, millets, & oilseeds, pulses) 2.0% of SI or Actuarial rate, whichever is less
Rabi Food & Oilseeds crops (all cereals, millets, & oilseeds, pulses) 1.5% of SI or Actuarial rate, whichever is less
Kharif & Rabi Annual Commercial / Annual Horticultural crops 5% of SI or Actuarial rate, whichever is less

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 6, para 10.1 Premium rates, maximum insurance charges payable by farmer (% of Sum Insured)

passages.text: The difference between premium rate and the rate of Insurance charges payable by farmers shall be treated as Rate of Normal Premium Subsidy, which shall be shared equally by the Centre and State.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; pp. 6-7, para 10.2 Premium subsidy

passages.text: Three levels of Indemnity, viz., 70%, 80% and 90% corresponding to crop Risk in the areas shall be available for all crops.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 9, para 13.1 Indemnity level

passages.text: For coverage through Banks:-The claim amount along with particulars will be released to the individual Nodal Banks. The Banks at the grass-root level, in turn, shall credit the accounts of the individual farmers and display the particulars of beneficiaries on their notice board.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 14, para 16.1 Settlement of claims

passages.text: For coverage through other insurance intermediaries: The claim amount will be released electronically to the individual Insured Bank Account.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 14, para 16.2 Settlement of claims

passages.text: The seasonality discipline shall be same for loanee and non-loanee farmers. The cut-off date is uniform for both loanee and non-loanee cultivators.

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; pp. 10-11, para 14 Calendar of activity

passages.text: Cut-off date for receipt of Proposals of farmers (loanee & non-loanee). 31th July 31st December

source.publisher: Department of Agriculture, Cooperation & Farmers Welfare, Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare, Government of India
source.locator: PMFBY scheme guidelines PDF; p. 11, para 14 Calendar of activity, cut-off date for proposals (Kharif, Rabi)

passages.text: All farmers, including tenant farmers and sharecroppers growing notified crops in notified areas.

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Eligibility, point 1

passages.text: Farmers must possess a valid and authenticated land ownership certificate or a valid land tenure agreement.

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Eligibility, point 3

passages.text: Farmers must not have received compensation for the same crop loss from any other medium or source.

passages.text:
Step 1: Visit the Official Website of "Pradhan Mantri Fasal Bima Yojana".
Step 2: At the top right corner of the homepage, click "Farmer Corner".
In the popup window, click "Guest Farmer". You will be taken to the Online Registration Form.
*If already registered, skip to Step: 4.

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Online via CSCs, steps 1-2

passages.text:
Step 3: In the Registration Form, fill in the following mandatory fields (marked with a red asterisk):
"FARMER DETAILS" Section: Full Name, Passbook Name, Relationship, Relative Name, Mobile No., Age, Caste Category, Gender, Farmer Type, Farmer Category,
"RESIDENTIAL DETAILS" Section: State, District, Sub District, Residential Village/ Town, Address, PIN Code
"FARMER ID" Section: ID Type, ID No,
"ACCOUNT DETAILS" Section: IFSC, Bank Name, Branch Name, Savings Bank A/C No., Confirm Savings Bank A/C No..
At the bottom of the registration form, fill in the Captcha Code and click "Create User".

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Online via CSCs, step 3

passages.text:
Step 4: Upon successful registration, click "Farmer Corner (Apply for Crop Insurance Yourself)".
In the popup window, click "Login for Farmer". You will be taken to the Login Page.

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Online via CSCs, step 4

passages.text: Step 5: On the Login Page, provide your Mobile Number, fill the Captcha Code, then click "Request for OTP". Enter the OTP received on your registered Mobile Number, and click "Submit". You will be taken to the "Farmer Application Form".

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Online via CSCs, step 5

passages.text:
Step 6: Fill in all the mandatory fields of the Application Form and upload all the mandatory documents in the specified format and size.
Click "Preview" to carefully review all the information provided and the uploaded documents. Click "Submit" to submit your application. You'll receive a confirmation message.

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Online via CSCs, step 6

passages.text:
Step 7: In the popup window, the following options will be displayed: "Pay Later" and "Make Payment". Select "Pay Later" if you intend to pay for the insurance at a later stage. Else, select "Make Payment".
Step 8: Upon successful payment, you may print the receipt of the payment.

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Application Process, Online via CSCs, steps 7-8

passages.text: You can track the application status on the PMFBY website through the ‘Application Status’ option on the home page.

source.publisher: Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare
source.locator: myScheme page; Track Your Application
